title: Daily X narrative digest — 2026-09-28

hits.name: Logan Kilpatrick
hits.text: 2027 is the year we will see at scale autonomous revenue (profit?) generating agents / mini-companies already happening at sub scale today with lots of rough edges
hits.hook: 2027 is the year we will see at scale autonomous revenue (profit?) generating agents / mini-companies already happening at sub scale today with lots of rough ed
hits.draft_en:
Autonomous revenue agents are not a 2030 slide. They are a messy 2026 side project with invoices.

Logan is calling 2027 the year of at-scale agent companies. The tell is the sub-scale mess already shipping: broken auth, flaky tools, weird edge cases, and somehow still collecting money.

If you wait for clean infrastructure, you will compete with people who already have ugly pipelines and real ARR.

Pick one boring cashflow loop. Wire an agent to the API. Measure profit per run, not demo applause.

Ship the rough edges. Charge before the polish.
hits.video_tip: 10-14s: glitchy agent dashboard ringing a cash register, caption ugly ARR > pretty demos.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text: I love this SaaS sales guy wants to do a call @halfdantimm hates calls so he says no Then he vibecodes his own replacement for free!
hits.hook: I love this SaaS sales guy wants to do a call @halfdantimm hates calls so he says no Then he vibecodes his own replacement for free!
hits.draft_en:
The best sales call is the one you delete by shipping the tool yourself.

SaaS wants a calendar link. Builders who hate calls open the editor and replace the product before the Zoom loads.

That is the new procurement: vibecode the wedge, keep the budget, own the roadmap.

If a vendor needs 3 discovery calls to explain pricing, ask what a weekend clone costs instead.

Refuse the call. Ship the replacement. Post the receipt.
hits.video_tip: 8-12s: calendar invite to trash to terminal green check shipped.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text:
I think every time AI can do something equally good or better than humans it stops being valuable or special

Marketing videos used to take lots of work of editing and motion graphics and a big budget

Now with Opus 5.5 etc it costs $0 to make one as good or better

That means
hits.hook: I think every time AI can do something equally good or better than humans it stops being valuable or special
hits.draft_en:
When AI matches human quality, the craft stops being the moat. Distribution and taste take the seat.

Marketing videos that ate budgets now fall out of Opus for near-zero cost. The scarce thing is not can we make it. It is who sees it, trusts it, and buys.

If your edge was production polish, you just got commoditized. If your edge is audience, offer, and iteration speed, you just got a free factory.

Audit what you still treat as special. Price the distribution, not the render.

Ship 10 variants today. Kill 9. Scale the winner.
hits.video_tip: 9-12s: expensive studio slate vs $0 AI render side-by-side, end card moat = distribution.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text:
I've now fully integrated my new site Hotelist into Hoodmaps

So now it lets you tap [ 🏨 Hotels ] and you see all available hotels in the area

You can hover over them or tap them and it'll show the same hover tooltip you see on Hotelist, and then when you tap again it opens the hotel

Nice to find a good area in a city and then book a place there

This was a recommendation by AI to try and monetize Hoodmaps, it gets almost 171,000 vistors per month but never made money in almost a decade, so I asked AI

It makes sense cause hotels are something aligned with when you're trying to find the best area in a city and it makes money!

It only shows when you click [ 🏨 Hotels ] though, so not annoying
hits.hook: I've now fully integrated my new site Hotelist into Hoodmaps
hits.draft_en:
171k monthly visitors and almost a decade of zero revenue is not a traffic problem. It is a monetization blind spot.

Levels asked AI how to make Hoodmaps pay. Answer: hotels, aligned with the exact moment someone is picking a neighborhood.

Traffic without a purchase moment is a hobby. Traffic with a native checkout is a business.

Look at your fun product. Name the one high-intent action already happening in the session. Attach money there, behind a toggle, not a popup war.

Ask the model for the monetization map. Ship the least annoying paid surface this week.
hits.video_tip: 12-16s: map pan, Hotels toggle, tooltip, book CTA, caption 171k visits to money.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text:
Lindt has an active lawsuit going against it for elevated levels of lead and cadmium

Most interestingly Lindt's lawyers themselves have suggested Lindt is not "expertly crafted" or "excellent" but that that is just advertising

So if even Lindt itself doesn't consider itself
hits.hook: Lindt has an active lawsuit going against it for elevated levels of lead and cadmium
hits.draft_en:
When a brand's own lawyers walk back expertly crafted, trust is the product and the product is on trial.

Levels highlighted Lindt's lead/cadmium suit and the lawyers undercutting the excellence claim. That is a content pattern: receipts beat slogans.

Builders can steal the structure. Find the gap between the marketing line and the legal footnote. Post the contrast with sources.

If you sell AI-powered excellence, assume someone will screenshot your disclaimer.

Ship receipts. Soft claims die in court and on timelines.
hits.video_tip: 8-11s: glossy ad claim hard cut to lawsuit PDF highlight, post the receipt.

hits.name: Tony Dinh
hits.text: You can do this on your own now. So cool.
hits.hook: You can do this on your own now. So cool.
hits.draft_en:
The unlock is not the tool drop. It is the sentence: you can do this on your own now.

Tony's short line travels because it hands agency back. No agency. No waitlist story. Just capability transferred.

For AI tools content, compress the demo into one proof the reader can repeat tonight.

If your post needs a 12-step funnel before the aha, you buried the product.

Show the before/after. End with you can run this tonight.
hits.video_tip: 6-9s: screen record one-click result, big caption you can do this on your own now.

hits.name: Alex Finn
hits.text: The most dangerous thing you can do right now is NOT use the latest AI tools. Period. Every day a new company is laying off thousands of people who don't know how to use the most modern AI tools If I were in the 9-5 world right now, this is every step I'd take: 1. Download Claude Code and build your first app using Opus 5.5. Learn how to implement a front end and database (I’d use nextJS and Convex). AI can teach you all of this 2. Download Grok Bot. Tell the agent about your entire life. Career, goals, and ambitions. Ask it which agents it can build and which workflows it can implement to get you closer to those goals. This is called reverse prompting. 3. Anytime you're about to do work manually, do it in Grok Bot instead. Tell Grok the task you need to do then ask it how it can do the task for you. You'll be surprised by how much of your work you can automate 4. Feed Astra 6 Max your hardest problems. Make sure you hit the rate limit on it EVERY single week 5. Constantly look at your limits in all your AI plans. If you're ever not above 50% on your limits, get angry that you're not burning enough tokens. 6. Start creating content and building a platform. Resumes no longer matter. Companies dont look at them anymore. They check your platform. What you talk about, what you’re passionate about, how you educate others, who follows you. This matters 100x more than anything else when getting hired right now. If you do these 6 things you are in excellent position to not only be safe in your career, but also dominate those that don't pick up these skills.
hits.hook: The most dangerous thing you can do right now is NOT use the latest AI tools. Period. Every day a new company is laying off thousands of people who don't know h
hits.draft_en:
The layoff risk is not AI exists. It is you still work like 2023.

Alex's checklist is blunt: Claude Code plus a real app, reverse-prompt your life into an agent desk, automate the manual loop, burn token limits on hard problems, build a public platform because resumes are dead weight.

The operators who win treat usage caps as a scoreboard, not a budget to protect.

If you are under 50% on your AI plan, you are training slower than your replacement.

Pick one workflow you did by hand yesterday. Agent it today. Post the artifact.
hits.video_tip: 12-18s: checklist stamps 1-6 on screen, end on burn the tokens / build the platform.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text: Also crazy you can see World War 1 and more so World War 2 in the histogram of hotels year built on hotelist.com
hits.hook: Also crazy you can see World War 1 and more so World War 2 in the histogram of hotels year built on hotelist.com
hits.draft_en:
Data products win when the chart makes history feel obvious.

A hotel year-built histogram that surfaces WW1 and WW2 is not trivia. It is a reason to keep clicking.

If your SaaS has a dataset, find the one visualization that makes strangers send screenshots.

Boring tables do not travel. Pattern recognition does.

Ship one chart that makes people say wait, zoom out.
hits.video_tip: 8-12s: histogram zoom revealing war-era spikes, caption your data has a plot twist.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text: Usually SaaS sales calls are to gauge how much you can spend and get you to spend the most money you could So it's like maximizing revenue and giving everyone a custom plan More good for businesses than for customers IMHO
hits.hook: Usually SaaS sales calls are to gauge how much you can spend and get you to spend the most money you could So it's like maximizing revenue and giving everyone a
hits.draft_en:
Custom SaaS pricing calls maximize their revenue, not your clarity.

Levels called it: the sales call is a spend-gauge. Great for the vendor. Taxing for the buyer.

Transparent tiers beat theater. If you need a call to learn the price, expect the price to discover you.

Builders: publish the number. Buyers: ask for the public plan before the calendar link.

Price on the page. Compete on product.
hits.video_tip: 7-10s: Book a demo button stamped REJECTED, clear public price card.

hits.name: Greg Isenberg
hits.text: There is an ENDLESS supply of intelligent people on the internet explaining why every opportunity is dead, every successful person got lucky, and everyone trying something new is too late, wrong or dumb. Don't listen. You deserve to share your ideas with the world.
hits.hook: There is an ENDLESS supply of intelligent people on the internet explaining why every opportunity is dead, every successful person got lucky, and everyone tryin
hits.draft_en:
The timeline has infinite smart people explaining why you are too late. That is not market research. That is cope at scale.

Greg's point: opportunity-killers sound intelligent. Builders sound naive until the screenshot of traction lands.

If you need permission from the cynics, you will never ship. If you need a customer, go talk to one.

Mute the autopsy threads. Publish the messy v1.

Share the idea before the chorus finishes explaining why it is dead.
hits.video_tip: 8-12s: scrolling too-late replies hard cut to shipped deploy, caption don't listen.

hits.name: Tony Dinh
hits.text: OMG this is so satisfying to peel
hits.hook: OMG this is so satisfying to peel
hits.draft_en:
Satisfying loops still print. Sensory demos are not below the AI lane when they stop the thumb.

Tony's peel post is a reminder: attention is a physical reaction first, a thesis second.

If your product has a delightful micro-interaction, film it raw. No essay. No stack flex.

Pair it later with the builder lesson. First, win the scroll.

Record the satisfying 3 seconds. Post it unpolished.
hits.video_tip: 5-8s: loop the peel/interaction, no voiceover, end card with product name only.

hits.name: Greg Isenberg
hits.text: I found my journal from the year 2000 (I was 11) "in the year 2010 there will be computers everywhere" Nobody knew "everywhere" would mean our phones, cars, doorbells etc The direction was obvious, but the details were impossible to see AI feels exactly like that right now!
hits.hook: I found my journal from the year 2000 (I was 11) "in the year 2010 there will be computers everywhere" Nobody knew "everywhere" would mean our phones, cars, doo
hits.draft_en:
In 2000 an 11-year-old wrote computers everywhere. He was right on direction and wrong on the form factor.

Greg's journal bit is the AI metaphor: phones, cars, doorbells were the invisible detail. Same fog now.

You do not need the perfect 2035 map. You need a bet on a surface that will be everywhere for your customer.

Direction is cheap. Distribution details are the work.

Write your 2026 journal line. Ship one product that assumes it is true.
hits.video_tip: 10-14s: kid journal close-up jump-cut phones/cars/doorbell, AI feels like that.

hits.name: Pieter Levels
hits.text: Vice versa, Hoodmaps was already integrated into Hotelist
hits.hook: Vice versa, Hoodmaps was already integrated into Hotelist
hits.draft_en:
Cross-embed the products that already share a user intent.

Hoodmaps inside Hotelist and Hotelist inside Hoodmaps is boring integration and smart monetization.

If two of your tools meet at the same decision moment, wire them both ways or leave money on the table.

Stop building islands. Build doors.

List your products. Draw the one shared intent. Ship the toggle.
hits.video_tip: 8-11s: two product UIs swapping embeds, caption vice versa.

hits.name: Yohei Nakajima
hits.text: who's got two thumbs and just ranked #6 of 49 on image-jevbench? 👍 this guy 👍 one of the fastest in top 10, accuracy is close. calibration of confidence is where it's weakest. @airesearch12 says a simple temperature fit should help so i'll need to look up what that means (thx!) try it out, it's all open-source! (current benchmark is on the frozen Qwen3-VL-4B via Glance)
hits.hook: who's got two thumbs and just ranked #6 of 49 on image-jevbench? 👍 this guy 👍 one of the fastest in top 10, accuracy is close. calibration of confidence is wher
hits.draft_en:
Public benchmarks are personal branding with a scoreboard.

Yohei posting #6/49 on image-jevbench with speed, accuracy, and a known weakness (confidence calibration) is the template: ship the number, name the gap, invite forks.

Closed leaderboards do not grow audiences. Open ones do.

If you have a model or agent trick, put it on a frozen baseline and post the rank.

Publish the score. Own the weakness. Link the repo.
hits.video_tip: 9-12s: leaderboard climb to #6, caption open-source or it did not happen.
